correctness.rationale: Direct expansion of the 2014 SAGA gradient-table update for identical scalar quadratic components yields x'= (1-s)x+s sigma v, u'=(x+u-sigma v)/2, v'=(v+sigma(x-u))/2. The explicit quadratic V_s has positive leading minor (s+2)/s, positive x-u block determinant 3s+2, and positive v coefficient 3s(s+1). Averaging the exact updates over both signs gives conditional drift (3s^2-4)x^2, checked by symbolic algebra and an exact-rational polynomial-identity checker. For s<2/sqrt(3), telescoping yields summable expected x-squares, while the cached-point averaging recurrences force their mean squares to zero. For s>=2/sqrt(3), expected V_s is nondecreasing, and mean-square iterate convergence would force all memory moments and V_s to zero, contradiction for every nonzero initial triple. Normalization s=eta L, equality case, quantifiers, and independence are explicit.

originality.rationale: The 2014 SAGA primary full text defines the control-variate update and gives general sufficient convergence guarantees but not this two-identical-component iff mean-square stability boundary or a conserved sharp-threshold energy. A later full SAGA stepsize paper optimizes expected-smoothness-derived guarantees, again not an all-initialization stochastic-recurrence necessity result. Extensive exact-form, alias, and cross-method searches found no implication-equivalent published claim. Residual risk is older specialized moment-operator or incremental-gradient analyses under alternate terminology; search incompleteness is not taken as novelty proof.

value.rationale: SAGA is a foundational variance-reduced optimizer, and stability limits govern permissible learning-rate tuning. Two identical scalar quadratic losses provide the most symmetric nontrivial SAGA dataset, so the strict penalty from 2 for deterministic gradient descent to 2/sqrt(3) is structurally informative rather than an arbitrary example: stochasticity arises solely from cached historical evaluations, not data heterogeneity. A sharp iff threshold with a positive-definite critical martingale provides a precise diagnostic for SAGA memory mechanisms, distinguishing necessary stability from the standard conservative sufficient stepsizes.
